plan: FICTIONAL EVALUATION FIXTURE. I'm adopting a two-year-old rescue dog next month, two weeks before a seven-day work trip. While I'm away the dog will stay at my sister's house, and she has agreed to look after it.

experts.objective: Health considerations of moving a newly adopted dog to another home shortly after adoption.
questions: What matters most for health & safety?

experts.objective: How a recently adopted rescue dog may cope with a second move after two weeks.
questions: What matters most for human & behavioral?

experts.objective: Practical arrangements for the week at the sister's house.
questions: What matters most for operations & logistics?

findings.title: Vaccination status and other animals at the sister's house
findings.observation: Depending on whether the sister's household has other animals, the dog's vaccination status could matter for staying there.
findings.why_it_matters: An unvaccinated dog sharing space with other animals could create a health risk for either.
assumptions: The sister's household may have other animals
The dog's vaccinations may not be complete

findings.title: Unknown health or medication needs
findings.observation: If the rescue dog has ongoing health conditions or medication, the sister would need to manage them for a week.
findings.why_it_matters: Missed medication or unnoticed symptoms would be harder to handle while you are away.
assumptions: The dog may have health needs not yet identified at adoption

assignment.objective: Health considerations of moving a newly adopted dog to another home shortly after adoption.
questions: What matters most for health & safety?

findings.title: Two weeks may be short to settle before another move
findings.observation: A rescue dog may still be adjusting after two weeks, so a move to a new house could add stress.
findings.why_it_matters: Stress can show up as hiding, not eating, or escape attempts in an unfamiliar place.
assumptions: The dog will not be settled within two weeks

findings.title: Separation-related behaviour is unknown
findings.observation: If the dog is anxious when left alone, time alone at the sister's house could lead to distress or damage.
findings.why_it_matters: It affects whether the dog can be left alone there and for how long.
assumptions: The sister will sometimes leave the dog alone

assignment.objective: How a recently adopted rescue dog may cope with a second move after two weeks.
questions: What matters most for human & behavioral?

findings.title: Daytime supervision at the sister's house
findings.observation: Depending on the sister's schedule, the dog may be alone for long stretches during the day.
findings.why_it_matters: Long periods alone can be hard for a newly adopted dog.
assumptions: The sister is away from home during working hours

findings.title: Getting the dog to and from the sister's house
findings.observation: The plan does not say how the dog will travel to the sister's house and back.
findings.why_it_matters: A stressful or unsecured journey could add to the dog's adjustment difficulties.
assumptions: The sister lives far enough away to need a car journey

assignment.objective: Practical arrangements for the week at the sister's house.
questions: What matters most for operations & logistics?
